The ship reached the island just after dawn, and for a long time no one on the deck said anything. Black cliffs rose straight out of the water, streaked with ice, and the surf broke against their base in slow white explosions. The research team had spent three weeks at sea to get here, crossing waters where the swells ran as high as a house. Now they stood in their orange survival suits, watching a small boat being lowered to carry the first group ashore. Penguins lined the rocky beach; thousands of them, shifting and calling in a roar that carried across the water. The lead scientist checked her equipment one more time: soil corers, a drone, a notebook wrapped in plastic. In a few hours they would begin counting nests, and the long work of the season would start.
